subject: Lightweight recap — load shape, token/sec clarity & next steps
messages:
From: Samir Khanna <samir@platformops.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@platformops.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Mar 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Quick sync — load shape & streaming needs

Evelyn, thanks for the intro call earlier — that was helpful. I wanted to capture the immediate asks from our side so your team can size and propose a sensible pilot.

Summary of what we said on the call:
- Primary workload: interactive support chat for customers (streaming responses with token-by-token delivery).
- Most important SLO: 95th percentile latency for streaming start should stay under ~350ms for the majority of requests.
- Typical day: low baseline traffic with short bursts tied to marketing pushes.

What we need from Redwood:
1) A short write-up of how you’d size for our workload (tokens/sec, QPS, and recommended concurrency for streaming sessions).
2) Clarify any tradeoffs (e.g., batching vs. latency for streaming).
3) A suggested mutual action plan / timeline for a 2-week pilot.

Attached an export of a 48-hour sample (summary rows only) so you can see crest windows.

Thanks — Samir

Attachment: customer_sample_load.csv (text/csv)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khanna <samir@platformops.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Mar 2028 15:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick sync — load shape & streaming needs

Samir — thanks for the tidy recap and for sending the sample. Internal summary and proposed next steps below.

Redwood's read (top-line):
- Baseline vs crest: sample shows sustained baseline ~30 r/s with short 10s crests up to ~230 r/s — aligns with what we discussed.
- Prompt/response sizes (need confirmation): if prompts are ~100–150 tokens and responses ~200–300 tokens, that maps to ~25–40k tokens/sec at crest if we assume no batching.
- Streaming behavior: continuous token streaming increases concurrency footprint (each open streaming session holds a KV cache + socket).

Sizing assumptions we’ll use for a quick pilot proposal:
- Average prompt: 120 tokens, average generated: 220 tokens.
- Average request processing time (network + server for first token): target p95 <= 350ms, p50 ~120ms.
- Streaming concurrency: assume 1.2x request concurrency factor for in-flight sessions due to long-generation tails.

Immediate next steps we propose:
1) Redwood to produce a short pilot sizing doc (tokens/sec, QPS, concurrent sessions) + cost delta between Hosted vs Dedicated for target SLO bands. (Deliverable: SLO_matrix.xlsx attached).
2) Redwood will sketch a fallback policy for crest events (model variant fallback + region routing) to protect p95.
3) Align on pilot window — we suggest a 2-week pilot in us-west with synthetic crest replaying from your sample.

I’ve attached our initial SLO matrix and a quick handback checklist for the pilot. Marissa and Karthik will follow up with the technical sizing details and a proposed pilot runbook.

Proposed timeline:
- This week: confirm pilot window and final sample fields we need (timestamps, request ids, avg token counts).
- By end of next week: deliver pilot sizing + cost estimate.
- Target pilot start: 2028-03-19 (flexible).

Thanks — looking forward to getting a small PoC running.

— Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: SLO_matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet), redwood-handback-checklist.pdf (application/pdf)

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/contact/78910
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khanna <samir@platformops.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Mar 2028 16:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick sync — load shape & streaming needs

Samir — quick technical follow-ups to make the size/cost estimate actionable. I’m dropping a short sizing note (attached) and a concise list of fields we need.

Fields we need from your sample (minimal): request_id, timestamp_iso, prompt_token_count, generated_token_count, is_streaming (boolean). If you can include 1–2 representative session traces (raw websocket session timestamps) that helps validate concurrency assumptions.

Sizing notes (high level):
- Tokens/sec vs QPS: for streaming workloads, tokens/sec matters more than QPS when sessions generate long outputs. Example calc for crest: 230 r/s * (120+220) tokens/request = 79,600 tokens/sec. With batching we can reduce GPU token cost by ~25–40% but batching increases first-token latency — important for your p95 target.
- Concurrency: assume each open streaming session consumes ~0.7–1.0 GB of host memory for KV + buffers depending on model. That means even modest bursts can hit rate-limits if sessions pile up.
- Latency knobs: we can meet p95 ~350ms with small batch windows (5–10ms) and prefix caching; if you need p95 <= 200ms we recommend Dedicated pools or a lower-precision quantized model variant.

Attached: sizing-notes.txt with a sample table and two scenario sketches (Hosted vs Dedicated). I’ll work with Karthik to put numbers into the SLO_matrix.xlsx Evelyn attached and send the completed matrix by COB Friday.

Marissa
Technical Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment: sizing-notes.txt (text/plain)
From: Samir Khanna <samir@platformops.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@platformops.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Mar 2028 17:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick sync — load shape & streaming needs

Thanks — all that is helpful. Quick answers from our side to unblock sizing:
- Confirmed averages for our dataset: prompt ~120 tokens, generated ~220 tokens (matches your assumption).
- Peak crest: we sometimes see ~10s windows with ~230 r/s; sustained peak for a few minutes up to ~45–60 r/s depending on campaign.
- Expected open streaming sessions: rough avg concurrency factor ~1.15 (we have fast closes, not long chat sessions).
- Region: prefer us-west.

Procurement note: copied procurement for contract/PO path. Procurement will send a short vendor form next week; they’re okay with a 2-week technical PoC before committing.

We’re good to proceed with the proposed timeline — confirm you’ll deliver the sizing + cost by EOW Friday and we’ll target a pilot start week of 2028-03-19.

Samir
PlatformOps Inc.

Attachment: procurement-sheet.pdf (application/pdf)
